disease_label_per_paper: Normocomplementemic urticarial vasculitis treated with omalizumab
presentation_summary: 57-year-old woman presented with wheals, arthralgias, and severe generalized burning sensation on the skin.
Lesions were urticarial plaques mainly on the trunk and proximal extremities, persisted more than 24 hours, and left faint residual hyperpigmentation.
She reported about 6 months of relapsing and remitting symptoms.
No angioedema or relevant past medical history was noted.
Laboratory tests were unremarkable, including normal complement levels.
Skin biopsy showed leukocytoclastic vasculitis with perivascular infiltrates and neutrophil predominance.
Initial treatment with oral corticosteroid course, H1 antihistamines, and hydroxychloroquine for 4 months did not improve symptoms.

Omalizumab 150 mg every 4 weeks was associated with improved UAS7 from 19 to 6 after 3 months; after later intermittent dosing, mean UAS7 after the ninth dose was 4.88 and she was asymptomatic without medication.
